*Pre-Assignment*
Load all necessary packages, read in the clinical data.csv file you have in your analysis_data folder, and instantiate the MAF_object.
```{r}
library(TCGAbiolinks)
library(maftools)

clinic <- read.csv(
  "~/490_cluster/analysis_data/brca_clinical_data.csv"
)
```

```{r}
"Tumor_Sample_Barcode" %in% names(clinic)
```
```{r}
query_maf <- GDCquery(
  project = "TCGA-BRCA",
  data.category = "Simple Nucleotide Variation",
  data.type = "Masked Somatic Mutation",
  access = "open",
  workflow.type =
    "Aliquot Ensemble Somatic Variant Merging and Masking"
)
```
```{r}
GDCdownload(
  query = query_maf,
  directory = "~/GDCdata",
  method = "api",
  files.per.chunk = 10
)
maf_data <- GDCprepare(
  query = query_maf,
  directory = "~/GDCdata"
)
```
```{r}
class(maf_data)
dim(maf_data)
head(maf_data)
```
```{r}
clinic$Tumor_Sample_Barcode <- substr(
  clinic$Tumor_Sample_Barcode,
  1,
  12
)

maf_data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode <- substr(
  maf_data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode,
  1,
  12
)
```
```{r}
length(
  intersect(
    unique(clinic$Tumor_Sample_Barcode),
    unique(maf_data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode)
  )
)
```
```{r}
MAF_object <- read.maf(
  maf = maf_data,
  clinicalData = clinic
)
```
```{r}
class(MAF_object)
MAF_object
slotNames(MAF_object)
```

It's useful to save your MAF_object, so that you don't have to go through the trouble of querying and preparing it everytime. The saveRDS function allows us to save an R object, allowing us to access it directly from our files. 
```{r}
data(MAF_object)
```

```{r}
saveRDS(
  MAF_object,
  file = "~/490_cluster/analysis_data/maf_object.rds"
)
```

When you reopen a new R session and want to access your MAF_object, you can use the readRDS function to load the object back into a new variable.
```{r}
MAF_object <- readRDS(file = "~/490_cluster/analysis_data/maf_object.rds")
```

*1*
Choose a clinical variable (or any variable from clin_rad or clin_drug) to separate your populations into two different groups and rewrite the column or create a new column with that variable as a factor. ***Do not use age or vital_status as your clinical variable.*** Hint: if your variable is continuous, you will need to determine your own cutoffs for the different levels of the factor. If your variable is categorical and has more than two possible values, choose the two that are the most common.
```{r}
colnames(MAF_object@clinical.data)
```
```{r}
MAF_object@clinical.data$menopause_status
```
```{r}
original_status <- as.character(
  MAF_object@clinical.data$menopause_status
)

clean_status <- sub(
  "\\s*\\(.*$",
  "",
  original_status
)

clean_status <- trimws(clean_status)
```

```{r}
MAF_object@clinical.data$factormenopause <- ifelse(clean_status == "Pre","Pre",ifelse(clean_status == "Post","Post",FALSE))
```
```{r}
View(MAF_object@clinical.data$factormenopause)
```

Research it. What is the gene used for? Can you think of any reason for the discrepancy?

```{r}

post_barcodes <- clinical$Tumor_Sample_Barcode[
```

```{r}

length(post_barcodes)
```

```{r}

  maf = MAF_object,

)

post_MAF <- subsetMaf(

  tsb = post_barcodes
)
```
```{r}
pre_MAF
post_MAF
```

*3*
Create a contingency table with your variable and chosen gene. Run a Fisher’s Exact Test between presence of mutations for that gene and your clinical variable. Create and save a mosaic plot. 
Interpret the output of the Fisher’s Exact Test in terms of the odds ratio and p-value.
```{r}
# Choose the gene identified in Step 2
target_gene <- "TP53"

# Unique patients with a mutation in the selected gene
mutated_barcodes <- unique(
  MAF_object@data$Tumor_Sample_Barcode[
    MAF_object@data$Hugo_Symbol == target_gene
  ]
)

# Count mutated and non-mutated patients in each group
pre_mutated <- sum(pre_barcodes %in% mutated_barcodes)
pre_not_mutated <- length(pre_barcodes) - pre_mutated

post_mutated <- sum(post_barcodes %in% mutated_barcodes)
post_not_mutated <- length(post_barcodes) - post_mutated
```

```{r}

mutation_table <- matrix(
  c(
    pre_mutated,
    pre_not_mutated,
    post_mutated,
    post_not_mutated
  ),
  nrow = 2,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(
    Menopause = c("Pre", "Post"),
    Mutation = c("Mutated", "Not_mutated")
  )
)

mutation_table
```

```{r}
mosaicplot(
  mutation_table,
  main = paste(target_gene, "Mutation by Menopause Status"),
  xlab = "Menopause Status",
  ylab = "Mutation Status",
  color = c("steelblue", "lightgray")
)
```

```{r}
graphics.off()

png("~/490_cluster/figures/contingency_table_for_menopause_status.png",
    width = 2400,
    height = 1400,
    res = 200)

mosaicplot(
  mutation_table,
  main = paste(target_gene, "Mutation by Menopause Status"),
  xlab = "Menopause Status",
  ylab = "Mutation Status",
  color = c("steelblue", "lightgray")
)

dev.off()
```
```{r}
fisher_result <- fisher.test(mutation_table)
fisher_result
```
#The odds ratio is 0.9976, which indicates that the odds of having mutated TP53 in pre menopause status is about 0.9976 times of the odds of having mutated PT53 in post menopause status.
#The p value is 1, which indicates that there is insufficient evidence to support the statistically significant correlation between TP53 gene mutation and menopause status.

*4*
Subset your maf_object based on your chosen clinical variable and create a co-lollipop plot of your chosen gene divided between the two different clinical variable possibilities. Include descriptive names on your plot.
Do you notice any difference in terms of mutations (e.g. sites, types, number) between the two populations?
#The overall mutation rates of each population are similar, and most of the mutations happen around the central p53 DNA-binding domain. The premenopausal group tends to have more sites with high mutation frequency in missense mutation, while the postmenopausal group has more nonsense mutations in the p53 domain. Also, the postmenopausal group has more mutations of the p53 tetramer than the premenopasual group.
```{r}
target_gene <- "TP53"   

maftools::lollipopPlot2(
  m1 = pre_MAF,
  m2 = post_MAF,
  gene = target_gene,
  AACol1 = "HGVSp_Short",
  AACol2 = "HGVSp_Short",
  m1_name = "Premenopausal",
  m2_name = "Postmenopausal"
)

```


```{r}
graphics.off()

png("~/490_cluster/figures/co-lollipop_plot_for_PT53_mutation_for_menopause_status.png",
```

*5*
Create your Overall_Survival_Status column and create a mafSurvival KM plot based on mutations in your chosen gene.
Does there seem to be a difference? Hypothesize why or not based on the other analysis you did with the gene above.
#There is insufficient evidence to support the statistical significance in the survival time between populations with and without TP53 mutation. Because the p value is 0.0858, which is greater than 0.05. Since TP53 is the gene with the highest mutation rates, we can not say the TP53 has no effect on the cancer and should collect more data for analysis.
```{r}
View(MAF_object@clinical.data)
```

```{r}
clinical$Overall_Survival_Status <- ifelse(
  clinical$vital_status == "Dead",
  TRUE,
  ifelse(clinical$vital_status == "Alive", FALSE, NA)
)

death_time <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(as.character(clinical$death_days_to))
)

followup_time <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(as.character(clinical$last_contact_days_to))
)

clinical$Overall_Survival_Time <- ifelse(
  clinical$Overall_Survival_Status == TRUE,
  death_time,
  followup_time
)
```
```{r}
table(clinical$Overall_Survival_Status, useNA = "ifany")
summary(clinical$Overall_Survival_Time)

sum(complete.cases(
  clinical$Overall_Survival_Time,
  clinical$Overall_Survival_Status
))
```

```{r}
maftools::mafSurvival(
  maf = MAF_object,
  clinicalData = clinical,
  genes = "TP53",
  time = "Overall_Survival_Time",
  Status = "Overall_Survival_Status",
  groupNames = c("TP53 Mutant", "TP53 Wild Type"),
  showConfInt = TRUE,
  addInfo = TRUE,
  col = c("pink", "skyblue"),
  isTCGA = FALSE
)
```
```{r}
sum(complete.cases(
  clinical$Overall_Survival_Time,
  clinical$Overall_Survival_Status
))
```
```{r}
graphics.off()

png("~/490_cluster/figures/KM_plot_of_TP53_Mutated_Wildtype.png",
    width = 2400,
    height = 1400,

    )

maftools::mafSurvival(

  groupNames = c("TP53 Mutant", "TP53 Wild Type"),
```
